About the Team
We use evolution to structure, explore, and engineer biology. Our Research team develops and experimentally validates new capabilities for biological discovery, prediction, and design. The primary focus of the team is to identify where new data would be most informative, develop computational and experimental methods for measuring and understanding biological variation, and determine through efficient, decisive tests whether these capabilities give Arcadia a meaningful scientific edge. We share our data, methods, and findings openly as the work develops.
The Opportunity
We’re hiring a Microscopy Machine Learning Scientist to develop methods that turn microscopy images into quantitative measurements of biology. You’ll work with colleagues who build imaging systems and design experiments, and you’ll help decide what to measure, what data to collect, and how to tell whether a model has captured a meaningful biological signal.
Our imaging research spans live-cell microscopy, quantitative phase imaging, and coherent Raman imaging. We’re interested in using these modalities to measure differences among cells, quantify how they change over time, and compare phenotypes across organisms. A central research question is how well those measurements carry across experimental batches, imaging conditions, and biological systems. You’ll identify where existing methods fall short, develop new approaches, and design experiments that test when they work.
You’ll be part of Arcadia’s research team and collaborate with our product development team to turn promising methods into tools that other researchers can use. This is an onsite role at our Emeryville, California headquarters, where daily proximity to researchers, engineers, and cross-functional partners keeps the feedback loop tight and the work grounded in real scientific need.
Key Responsibilities
Develop and benchmark machine learning methods for microscopy. Depending on the scientific question, projects could include learning representations from label-free images, segmenting and tracking live cells, or combining measurements from multiple imaging modalities.
Work with experimental scientists to design data collection, select biological controls, and decide which annotations or independent measurements are needed to evaluate a model.
Test whether models generalize across batches, imaging conditions, and organisms. Investigate which image features drive predictions and whether they reflect the biology of interest.
Build reproducible pipelines for image preprocessing, model training, evaluation, and inference. Work with the product development team to make successful methods usable at scale.
Share findings through open publications, documented code, and reusable analysis workflows.
Qualifications
Required
PhD in machine learning, computer vision, computational biology, bioengineering, biophysics, or a related quantitative field.
Research experience developing or substantially adapting machine learning methods for microscopy or closely related scientific imaging data.
Ability to take a research question from problem formulation through implementation, benchmarking, and interpretation.
Experience designing evaluations that account for dependencies in experimental data, such as images from the same specimen, well, or acquisition batch.
Ability to write reliable research software, with attention to testing, documentation, and reproducibility.
Ability to work independently and communicate technical findings clearly to experimental and computational collaborators.
Preferred
Experience with live-cell microscopy, quantitative phase imaging, coherent Raman imaging, fluorescence microscopy, or other forms of quantitative microscopy.
Experience with self-supervised learning, learning from limited annotations, multimodal image analysis, or modeling time-lapse data.
Experience collaborating on microscopy acquisition or experimental design, including diagnosing artifacts and sources of variability.
Postdoctoral or industry research experience, including in a startup or other interdisciplinary research environment.
A record of open science contributions, such as published code, datasets, benchmarks, or reusable analysis pipelines.
Compensation
Successful applicants can expect to be compensated between $160,000-$200,000 with benefits and a competitive equity offering, depending on experience level.
Application Process
Please submit a resume and fully answer all application questions addressing your interest in and qualifications for the position. The review process will involve in-person interviews and a short, practical work test. Employment offers are contingent on reference and background checks.
Arcadia is an equal opportunity workplace; we welcome people from all backgrounds and communities. We provide competitive compensation and practical benefits to keep you happy and healthy so that you can do your best work.
